currentContext.business: Shilchar Technologies has manufactured transformer solutions since 1986 and today produces transformers up to 50 MVA and 132 KV class from a single integrated facility at Gavasad, Vadodara. It serves renewable energy (solar, wind and hydro), industrial and specialised applications including furnace and converter duty, selling to private utilities, renewable developers, cement, sugar, steel and hydrocarbon industries, large-scale EPC contractors and power plant developers. The company began with R-core transformers in 1986, added Ferrite transformers in 1995, and entered Power and Distribution transformers between 2004 and 2007.

currentContext.strategies: Execute Gavasad Expansion #3, the largest capacity expansion in the Company's history, adding 6,500 MVA to take installed capacity to 14,000 MVA, funded entirely from internal accruals without external borrowings|Move up the voltage ladder by extending capability into the 220 kV class for the first time, opening the larger market for higher-voltage power transformers and widening the customer base beyond the current 50 MVA / 132 kV range|Run existing 7,500 MVA capacity at close to full utilisation in FY27, with the new capacity coming onstream in April 2027 to drive the next phase of growth from FY28 as higher-voltage approvals are secured and new lines fill with orders|Retain optionality for further brownfield growth: the Gavasad site has further land available beyond 14,000 MVA, allowing capacity to keep being added at the same site as demand grows|Sustain leadership in renewable-application transformers, supplying inverter duty transformers for solar projects and generator transformers for wind projects|Maintain a debt-free balance sheet with substantial cash reserves so the entire expansion programme is self-funded|Broaden the export base across the 25+ countries served, with export disruptions treated as temporary and price revisions used to restore margins|Preserve a made-to-order model built on deep engineering capability and consistent delivery, sustaining repeat-supplier status with customers across cycles|Maintain discipline across design, procurement and production as the stated source of consistent execution|The Company operates on a zero-debt, self-funded model: it maintains a debt-free balance sheet with substantial cash reserves, which it states enable strategic investments in growth, capacity expansion and technology, and it is funding the Gavasad Expansion #3 entirely through internal accruals rather than external borrowings. On distributions, the stated intent is to maintain the continuity of the Company's proven track record of declaring dividends, and the Board recommended a final dividend of 125% on the paid-up equity share capital for FY 2025-2026 for approval by Members at the 40th AGM. currentContext.expansion: Shilchar's single manufacturing site at Gavasad spans 17 acres and currently carries an annual production capacity of 7,500 MVA, of which close to 79% was utilised during FY26. During FY26 the Company commenced the largest capacity expansion in its history, the Gavasad Expansion #3 project, a new 6,500 MVA facility that will take total installed capacity to 14,000 MVA by April 2027. The expansion is funded entirely through internal accruals, consistent with the Company's zero-debt balance sheet and substantial cash reserves. Beyond volume, the project is a capability step-up: it adds 220 kV class capability to the product range for the first time, versus the current ceiling of transformers up to 50 MVA and 132 KV class, enabling Shilchar to address a larger segment of the market. On the ramp path, management expects to operate at full utilisation of the existing 7,500 MVA capacity in FY27, with the new capacity coming onstream from FY28. Looking further out, the Company states that with planned capacity expansions it aims to scale manufacturing capabilities to 25,000-30,000 MVA in the coming years. The Company has no subsidiaries, joint ventures or additional sites disclosed in this section, and there is no change in the nature of its business during the financial year.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility in CRGO steel and copper
risks.note: Movements in the prices of cold-rolled grain-oriented steel and copper can affect profitability. The Company states much of the impact is mitigated through variable pricing contracts linked to the IEEMA index, but the exposure is structural to a transformer manufacturer's cost base.

BRSR discloses that 100% of turnover comes from a single business activity (electric power generation, transmission and distribution) and 100% from a single product line, Power & Distribution Transformers. There is no product or segment diversification to absorb a downturn in the transformer cycle.

risks.risk: High export dependence and geopolitical/trade disruption
risks.note: Exports contribute 48.31% of total turnover. Global trade tensions, the Middle East conflict from end-February 2026 and associated supply-chain disruptions are explicitly cited as forces reshaping the macro backdrop, and the IMF flags further escalation of trade tensions as a downside risk. A concentrated export book is therefore exposed to events entirely outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Supply-chain lead times for critical inputs
risks.note: Extended lead times for critical inputs and components can influence project timelines, an industry-level challenge that directly affects the Company's ability to convert orders into dispatches.

risks.risk: Execution bandwidth as the industry migrates to higher-voltage equipment
risks.note: The shift towards higher-voltage equipment, while positive for value, may continue to influence the pace of order execution in the near term. Sector-level ordering already moderated during FY26 owing primarily to execution-bandwidth constraints and longer lead times for higher-kV equipment. This is directly relevant given the Company's own move into the 220 kV class.

Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a Risk with negative financial implications, given transformer manufacturing involves heavy equipment, high-voltage testing and material handling. Mitigated through safety protocols, regular training, statutory compliance, continuous monitoring, risk assessments and employee feedback mechanisms.

The Indian rupee depreciated to an all-time low of approximately Rs 95/USD by end-March 2026 on foreign portfolio outflows and market volatility following the Middle East crises, and higher oil and gas import costs are expected to raise inflationary pressures. For an exporter that also imports key inputs, this cuts both ways on realisations and cost.

The BRSR discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 28.38% in FY 25-26, broadly in line with 28.57% in FY 24-25 and 24.49% in FY 23-24. Sustained attrition near 28% is a structural human-capital risk for a made-to-order engineering business, even as permanent-worker turnover was nil.
Meeting stringent quality and regulatory requirements adds to production complexity and cost, and higher voltage classes require fresh approvals before new lines can be commercially loaded.

one-line thesis: Debt-free, high-margin (~29%) niche transformer maker riding India grid + renewables capex and US/Middle East export demand; FY26 growth muted (+5%) by transient West Asia shipping crisis and oil/RM inflation, with a step-change in capacity (7,500 → 14,000 MVA) setting up multiple growth from FY28.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue from ops | INR 152 cr | INR 652 cr | ~+5% | ~INR 35–40 cr (mgmt also said INR 70–80 cr / INR 75 cr) of Middle East exports undispatched in March due to West Asia crisis |
| EBITDA / margin | margin ~21% | INR 190 cr / 29% | — | Q4 margin hit ~7–8 pts vs prior quarters (lower high-margin exports + RM/oil inflation) |

5-yr CAGR: Revenue 38%, EBITDA 77%, PAT 83%. Q4 export INR 52 cr vs domestic ~INR 100 cr. Inventory ~INR 100 cr at FY-end (incl. WIP, similar to FY25 INR 92 cr because production was halted when shipping stopped).
guidance (next quarter / fy27):
- FY27 revenue: INR 800 cr (conservative; "can reach INR 900 cr"; prior calls had floated INR 850–900 cr — now toned down). Confident on INR 800 cr.
- Q1 FY27: "a normal quarter"; declined to give April actuals. Shipping to Middle East resumed in April; US order intake/deliveries picked up in Q1 FY27.
- FY27 EBITDA margin: targeting to maintain or improve 29–31%.
- FY27 volume: ~7,000 MVA dispatches (vs ~6,000 MVA in FY26); aiming for 90–95% utilization.
order book & pipeline:
- Current order book INR 452 cr; ~30–32% export.
- FY27 order visibility ~INR 800 cr, robust domestic + export inquiries.
- Lower export mix vs historical is purely a dispatch (West Asia) issue, not demand loss — deferred, not cancelled.
- Power transformer lead time 12–16 weeks.
segment / subsidiary: Standalone entity, no subsidiaries discussed. Mix: distribution transformers (domestic, firm demand), inverter duty transformers (IDT) for solar/wind, power transformers. Geographic: domestic ~firm; Middle East ~30% of FY26 revenue; US ~18–19% of FY26 revenue.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **220 kV / 160 MVA class** power transformers via new Gavasad-3 facility — new higher-voltage segment; will pursue PGCIL and customer approvals (audits) once facility ready.
- IDT (inverter duty transformers) for India renewables (govt target 50–55 GW RE) and Middle East.
- US export ramp as 50% tariff fell to 10% — "opportunities in next 3 years going to be great."
- New facility to be kept busy initially with solar/wind transformers, then shift toward power transformers as approvals come — flexible asset utilization.
- Path to ~INR 1,500 cr turnover at full utilization of expanded capacity; further expansion already contemplated.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Q4 gross/EBITDA margin compressed ~7–8 pts. Two drivers: (a) lower share of higher-margin exports (Middle East dispatch halt), (b) RM inflation — transformer oil up ~100% since Feb; other commodities (copper, aluminium, steel) up 10–25%.
- Oil is 8–12% of transformer cost.
- Price-hike strategy: approaching all customers (force majeure basis) for revision on fixed-price orders; some already agreed and supply resumed. Orders with PV (price-variation/EMA) clause auto-adjust at dispatch. New inquiries quoted at current RM cost — no future margin impact expected. Rupee depreciation on imports also a minor pressure.
- Normally hedges copper/aluminium at order booking; this episode was a supplier-side force-majeure where even booked material repriced.
capex / expansion:
- Gavasad Expansion-3: adds 6,500 MVA → total 14,000 MVA. Commissioning April '27.
- Capex ~INR 120 cr, fully funded by internal accruals.
- Status: civil foundation done; PEB erection + utility infra in progress; all major production equipment ordered.
- Existing 7,500 MVA to run near full util in FY27; new facility drives growth FY28 onward; full impact FY29–FY30.
capital allocation: - Debt-free; cash INR 246 cr (part funds capex). FY26 OCF INR 192 cr. Capex self-funded via internal accruals. No buyback/dividend specifics discussed on call. Further capacity expansion to be announced in future.
risks & watch-items:
- **RM inflation pass-through**: success of price-hike negotiations on existing fixed-price order book is the swing factor for FY27 margins; domestic customers' willingness to absorb is uncertain (mgmt confident).
- **Geopolitics/logistics**: West Asia (Strait of Hormuz) shipping disruption directly hit Q4; recurrence risk for ~30% Middle East revenue.
- **US tariff policy**: volatile (50% → 10%); past order losses; remains a macro variable.
- **Industry capacity addition**: many transformer players expanding simultaneously — demand-absorption risk if grid/RE demand softens; competition in lower-kV class.
- **Bushing supply**: industry shortage; long lead times for 220 kV; dependent on Yash Highvoltage (code unverified) + China imports.
- **Approval timeline risk**: PGCIL/customer audits could delay 220 kV power-transformer ramp.
management quality / tone: Candid and conservative. Owns the weak Q4, attributes to two clearly external/transient factors (West Asia logistics, RM spike) without spin. Track record of beating own guidance ("whatever figure we said, we have always done more"). Honest about not predicting commodity prices and about utilization-on-dispatch vs production nuance (Pokharna clarification). Conservative on guidance (INR 800 vs prior INR 850–900). Tone confident but measured.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported FY26 "capacity utilization" (79%) is on a **dispatch** basis; **production** was higher (FG held as closing stock) — true operating run-rate stronger than headline. This is the key reconciliation analysts missed.
- The INR 35–40 cr undispatched export is also quoted as INR 70–80 cr / INR 75 cr in different exchanges — magnitude of the Q4 "miss" is ambiguous; on a like-for-like add-back FY26 would have been ~INR 700 cr (vs INR 623 cr prior year).
- New facility deliberately flexible: solar/wind transformers fill it pre-approval, swap to power transformers post-approval — de-risks the ramp.
- FY27 INR 800 cr top-line implies ~95–100% utilization at current ~INR 11 lakh/MVA realization, i.e. limited volume headroom until FY28 — most of FY27 "growth" may be price-led, not volume-led.

- Guidance trimmed: prior calls indicated FY27 INR 850–900 cr; now conservatively INR 800 cr (still allows up to INR 900 cr).
- Q4 FY26 a clear sequential miss: revenue INR 152 cr and EBITDA margin ~21% (vs ~29% normalized), driven by West Asia dispatch halt + oil/commodity spike — both flagged transient.
- New disclosure: ~INR 35–40 cr (also cited as INR 70–80 cr) Middle East exports deferred from March to April FY27; shipping resumed April.
- US tariff normalized 50% → 10% vs prior-quarter uncertainty; US orders resumed in Q1 FY27.
- New RM shock: transformer oil ~+100% since February (not present in prior calls); broad commodity inflation 10–25%.
- Capex update: Gavasad-3 (6,500 MVA, → 14,000 MVA total) civil done, equipment ordered, on track for April '27; INR 120 cr internally funded.
- New capability disclosed: new facility to make up to 220 kV / 160 MVA class (vs current 132 kV cap), pending approvals.
- Order book INR 452 cr (current), ~30–32% export. Cash INR 246 cr, debt-free; FY26 OCF INR 192 cr.

capital allocation: - Debt-free; cash INR 246 cr (part funds capex). FY26 OCF INR 192 cr. Capex self-funded via internal accruals. No buyback/dividend specifics discussed on call. Further capacity expansion to be announced in future.
risks & watch-items:
- **RM inflation pass-through**: success of price-hike negotiations on existing fixed-price order book is the swing factor for FY27 margins; domestic customers' willingness to absorb is uncertain (mgmt confident).
- **Geopolitics/logistics**: West Asia (Strait of Hormuz) shipping disruption directly hit Q4; recurrence risk for ~30% Middle East revenue.
- **US tariff policy**: volatile (50% → 10%); past order losses; remains a macro variable.
- **Industry capacity addition**: many transformer players expanding simultaneously — demand-absorption risk if grid/RE demand softens; competition in lower-kV class.
- **Bushing supply**: industry shortage; long lead times for 220 kV; dependent on Yash Highvoltage (code unverified) + China imports.
- **Approval timeline risk**: PGCIL/customer audits could delay 220 kV power-transformer ramp.
management quality / tone: Candid and conservative. Owns the weak Q4, attributes to two clearly external/transient factors (West Asia logistics, RM spike) without spin. Track record of beating own guidance ("whatever figure we said, we have always done more"). Honest about not predicting commodity prices and about utilization-on-dispatch vs production nuance (Pokharna clarification). Conservative on guidance (INR 800 vs prior INR 850–900). Tone confident but measured.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported FY26 "capacity utilization" (79%) is on a **dispatch** basis; **production** was higher (FG held as closing stock) — true operating run-rate stronger than headline. This is the key reconciliation analysts missed.
- The INR 35–40 cr undispatched export is also quoted as INR 70–80 cr / INR 75 cr in different exchanges — magnitude of the Q4 "miss" is ambiguous; on a like-for-like add-back FY26 would have been ~INR 700 cr (vs INR 623 cr prior year).
- New facility deliberately flexible: solar/wind transformers fill it pre-approval, swap to power transformers post-approval — de-risks the ramp.
- FY27 INR 800 cr top-line implies ~95–100% utilization at current ~INR 11 lakh/MVA realization, i.e. limited volume headroom until FY28 — most of FY27 "growth" may be price-led, not volume-led.

qoq change log:
- Guidance trimmed: prior calls indicated FY27 INR 850–900 cr; now conservatively INR 800 cr (still allows up to INR 900 cr).
- Q4 FY26 a clear sequential miss: revenue INR 152 cr and EBITDA margin ~21% (vs ~29% normalized), driven by West Asia dispatch halt + oil/commodity spike — both flagged transient.
- New disclosure: ~INR 35–40 cr (also cited as INR 70–80 cr) Middle East exports deferred from March to April FY27; shipping resumed April.
- US tariff normalized 50% → 10% vs prior-quarter uncertainty; US orders resumed in Q1 FY27.
- New RM shock: transformer oil ~+100% since February (not present in prior calls); broad commodity inflation 10–25%.
- Capex update: Gavasad-3 (6,500 MVA, → 14,000 MVA total) civil done, equipment ordered, on track for April '27; INR 120 cr internally funded.
- New capability disclosed: new facility to make up to 220 kV / 160 MVA class (vs current 132 kV cap), pending approvals.
- Order book INR 452 cr (current), ~30–32% export. Cash INR 246 cr, debt-free; FY26 OCF INR 192 cr.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.
